Article Title: Google cofounder Sergey Brin has donated $100 million, more than any billionaire, opposing California's Wealth Tax, but he cannot cast a vote next month as ...
Article Text:
Sergey Brin’s move to Nevada linked to tax concerns

What is California's Proposition 40

Billionaires and Gavin Newsom line up against it

Larry Page also shifts residency

Google cofounder Sergey Brin has emerged as the biggest financial opponent of California’s proposed billionaire wealth tax, contributing more than $100 million to campaigns against the measure. However, the tech billionaire will not be eligible to vote on the proposal next month after changing his voter registration from California to Nevada, according to a Forbes report. Brin has channelled his opposition to the tax through his Build a Better California PAC, making him the largest donor fighting the initiative. The irony, Forbes noted, is that Brin himself will not get a say at the ballot box because public records from the Nevada Secretary of State's office show he changed his voter registration to Nevada on December 10.According to Forbes, Brin's relocation appears to be part of a broader effort to avoid the proposed tax, which would apply only to California residents as of January 1, 2026.The billionaire purchased a $42 million mansion on the Nevada side of Lake Tahoe in December, and his representatives told Forbes that he is now a Nevada resident.The move also makes Brin, whose net worth is estimated at $263 billion, the richest resident of Nevada, surpassing casino heiress and Republican donor Miriam Adelson, whose fortune is estimated at $31.2 billion.Brin's voter registration reportedly lists his political affiliation as nonpartisan.Proposition 40 will be on the ballot in November. It would impose a one-time 5% tax on California’s 200 billionaires. Ninety percent of the revenue would go to the state’s health care program. The remaining 10% would go to education, food assistance and administration. With a net worth of nearly $260 billion, Brin could owe about $13 billion if it passes.Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel have also donated to groups opposing the measure. Brin has likened the proposal to the socialist society he left behind. “I fled socialism with my family in 1979,” he told The New York Times in April, adding that he does not want California to end up in the same place.Gov. Gavin Newsom has also come out against the tax. He argues it would erode the state’s tax base and cut revenue for social services. In an interview with Bloomberg Businessweek earlier this year, he said it would reduce investment in education, teachers, librarians, childcare, firefighting and police.Forbes reported that Brin's Google cofounder Larry Page has likewise moved away from California, although he is not yet registered to vote in Florida, according to records reviewed by the publication.Page's representatives told Forbes that his residency has changed from California to Florida. The billionaire reportedly spent $173 million on two Miami mansions between December 2025 and January 2026. With an estimated net worth of $286 billion, Page is now said to be the second-richest resident of Florida, behind Jeff Bezos, whose fortune is estimated at $374 billion.Representatives for both Brin and Page did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding their voter registration status, Forbes said.
Article Summary: Google cofounder Sergey Brin changed his voter registration from California to Nevada on December 10. His net worth is estimated at $263 billion, making him the richest resident of Nevada. Brin has channelled his opposition to the tax through his Build a Better California PAC. His Google cofounder Larry Page has likewise moved away from California, although he is not yet registered to vote in Florida.

Article Title: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang reveals the man who made the 'impossible' possible between Apple and Meta
Article Text:
Tim Cook-Mark Zuckerberg once clashed over privacy

Meta's most capable open AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio

Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang has revealed that former Apple executive Daniel Gross played a key role in bringing the iPhone-maker and Meta together for an AI collaboration. After years of disagreements, the two companies are now working together to run Meta's new Muse Spark Open AI model on Apple's high-end Mac Studio computers. Their collaboration allows Muse Spark Open, which has 816 billion parameters, to run across two or four connected Mac Studios powered by Apple's M5 Ultra chips, using Apple's MLX framework. Alexandr Wang told Axios that Gross, who now works at Meta, helped the two sides work together. Wang revealed that the two companies had been working together for several months.“I think he played a really big role in kind of getting the two companies to work nicely together,” Alexandr Wang told the publication. “We're excited for mommy and daddy to be playing nice again,” he said.The rivalry between Apple and Meta (then Facebook) dates back to 2018 during the Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal. The then Apple CEO Tim Cook was asked what he would do if he were Mark Zuckerberg. Tim Cook then replied saying “I wouldn't be in this situation”.Later, Mark Zuckerberg called Cook's comments "extremely glib.” Again in 2021, when Apple introduced new privacy protections, Zuckerberg told employees that Facebook needed to "inflict pain" on Apple over the dispute, per a report by the Wall Street Journal then.Muse Spark Open is an 816-billion-parameter model built on a mixture-of-experts design. Meta calls it the most capable US-developed open-weight model to date. It is aimed at long coding sessions, multi-step reasoning and video analysis. The model is free to download from platforms like Hugging Face, and its licence allows commercial use with some limits.The setup links two or four Mac Studios running Apple's M5 Ultra chip. Apple's MLX framework splits the model across those machines. Apple has also put out new benchmarks and technical notes on how MLX handles open models of this size. Since everything stays on the desk, Meta does not see the prompts or files developers feed it. "Meta has no control or visibility to any of that," Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said.It does not come cheap. An M5 Ultra Mac Studio with 256GB of memory costs over Rs 9 lakh at US prices, and the model needs at least two. A 512GB version is due later this month.
Article Summary: Meta's Muse Spark Open AI model now runs on Apple's Mac Studio computers. Former Apple executive Daniel Gross played a key role in bringing the two companies together for an AI collaboration. The rivalry between Apple and Meta dates back to 2018 during the Facebook's Cambridge Analytica scandal.

Article Title: What is CXMT's 'Chinese chip bomb' that has wiped billions off the US stock market
Article Text:
One Chinese chip design, billions gone from Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung (Picture: Reuters)

CXMT's 4F² chip design squeezes more memory into less space

Why Micron and SK Hynix have so much to lose right now

CXMT still has no answer to HBM, the memory inside AI chips

A Chinese memory chipmaker that few investors outside China had heard of until this summer has spent the past week knocking billions of dollars off the world's biggest chip stocks. ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, says it has made "key progress" on a denser memory chip design, and the news has sent Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung and a string of storage companies sharply lower.The worry is specific. CXMT plans to bring a server memory module built on the new design to market by the end of 2026, aiming straight at the part of the memory business where AI demand has pushed prices and profits to record highs. SK Hynix fell more than 10% in Seoul on Tuesday, Samsung dropped 7.4% and South Korea's Kospi lost 5.5%. In the US, the Philadelphia semiconductor index slid for a fifth straight session, with Micron, Seagate and Western Digital among the hardest hit.CXMT president Cao Kanyu outlined the plan at an industry event in Shanghai on October 10. The technology is called 4F², also written as 4F square, where F is the smallest feature a chipmaker can print on silicon.Mainstream DRAM cells today take up about 6F². Cutting that to 4F² shrinks each cell by roughly a third, which in theory fits 50% more cells into the same area.The first product will be a DDR5 RDIMM, the memory module that sits inside data centre servers. CXMT credits a vertical transistor design that keeps electrical leakage in check as cells get smaller.Samsung and SK Hynix are chasing the same architecture, and SK Hynix published a roadmap for it last year. A Chinese rival widely seen as a step behind claiming progress first is what rattled the market.Memory has been the most profitable corner of the AI boom this year. Micron's revenue for the quarter ended September jumped to $54.23 billion from $11.32 billion a year earlier, and its gross margin climbed to 86.8%. Those numbers rest on a shortage, so even the prospect of a new supplier puts that pricing power in question.CXMT is no small player either. HSBC estimates its share of the global DRAM market has grown to about 10%, from roughly 4% a year ago. The Hefei-based company raised $8.6 billion in Asia's biggest IPO of the year in July. On Friday, it reported preliminary nine-month profit of up to 132.5 billion yuan (about $19.8 billion), against a loss of 5.3 billion yuan a year earlier.Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth, called it profit-taking, noting that when competition looms, "all the sheep run to the door at the same time." Broadcom CEO Hock Tan comparing AI spending to gambling a day earlier did little for the mood.Several analysts think the selloff ran ahead of reality. CXMT has not shown it can make the new chips in volume, and server customers take months to approve a new supplier. The plan also leaves out high-bandwidth memory, or HBM, the stacked memory that sits next to Nvidia's AI processors, where SK Hynix and Samsung remain far ahead. US export controls keep the most advanced chipmaking machines out of China too.Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra still expects demand to outrun supply through 2027 and 2028, with more than three-quarters of next year's output already spoken for.The chip index is up over 70% this year, which leaves plenty of room for nervous selling. Whether CXMT's design becomes a real threat will be clear once its first server modules reach customers around the end of the year.
Article Summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies, or CXMT, says it has made "key progress" on a denser memory chip design. The news has sent Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung and a string of storage companies sharply lower. CX MT plans to bring a server memory module built on the new design to market by 2026.

Article Title: Canadian billionaire Kevin O Leary: Till few years ago, I always told everyone that the only education you should get is Engineering, Engineering, and Engineering; but no longer as now the highest-pai
Article Text:
Kevin O’Leary: I don’t believe in only engineering anymore

Kevin’O Leary believes creators changing how businesses find customers

What 'O Leary means

'Amazing what's happening to the arts'

Read Kevin O’Leary’s post here

I used to say just a few years ago, the only education you should get is engineering, engineering, and engineering. I don't believe that anymore because storytelling, photography, video editing, and creators, are changing the landscape for both large and small businesses by acquiring customers. It's not a $48,000 career anymore, it's more like a $400,000 career because they’re doing the contracts with multiple companies, showing them how to reduce their customer acquisition cost and increase their return on ad spend.

That's the opportunity. It's amazing what's happening to the arts.

Canadian billionaire and Shark Tank Judge Kevin O’Leary has said he no longer believes engineering is the only educational path that guarantees career success, arguing that storytelling and digital content creation have emerged among the most lucrative skills in today's economy. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), O'Leary said his views on education and high-demand careers have shifted significantly over the past few years as businesses increasingly rely on creators and digital marketers to acquire customers and grow revenue."I used to say just a few years ago, the only education you should get is engineering, engineering, and engineering. I don't believe that anymore," O'Leary wrote. According to O'Leary, skills such as storytelling, photography and video editing are reshaping the way both large and small companies attract customers. He said creators are becoming essential business partners because they help brands lower customer acquisition costs and improve returns on advertising spending.O’Leary said storytelling, photography, video editing and content creation are reshaping the landscape for both large and small businesses by helping them acquire customers.“It’s not a $48,000 career anymore, it’s more like a $400,000 career because they’re doing the contracts with multiple companies,” he said. He added that creators are showing companies how to reduce their customer acquisition cost and increase their return on ad spend. “That’s the opportunity,” he said. He ended with a nod to the creative fields: “It’s amazing what’s happening to the arts.”Customer acquisition cost is how much a business spends to win one new customer. Return on ad spend measures the revenue earned for every dollar spent on advertising. O’Leary’s argument is that creators who can produce content that brings in customers cheaply are being paid by several companies at once, rather than working for a single employer on a fixed salary. The $48,000 and $400,000 figures are O’Leary’s own and were not accompanied by a source. He did not say what group of workers they refer to or whether the higher number represents typical or top-end earnings.O'Leary said the growing demand for content creators highlights a broader shift in the economy, where creative professionals are increasingly driving business growth."That's the opportunity. It's amazing what's happening to the arts," he said.
Article Summary: Kevin O'Leary says storytelling, photography, video editing and content creation are reshaping the landscape for both large and small businesses by helping them acquire customers. He said creators are becoming essential business partners because they help brands lower customer acquisition costs and improve returns on advertising spending.

Article Title: Federal Bank appoints Cognizant executive Rajesh Varrier as independent director
Article Text: Private sector lender Federal Bank has appointed Rajesh Varrier, president of global operations and CMD, Cognizant India, as an Additional Director in the capacity of a Non-Executive Independent Director on its board for a three-year term beginning October 16, 2026.The appointment was approved by the bank's Board of Directors at its meeting held on October 16, 2026, following the recommendations of the Nomination, Remuneration, Ethics and Compensation Committee. The appointment has been made in accordance with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025.In a regulatory filing, Federal Bank said Varrier will serve as an Additional Director (Non-Executive Independent Director) for a period of three consecutive years with effect from October 16, 2026.As required under Regulation 17(1C) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the bank will seek shareholder approval for the appointment at the next general meeting or within three months from the date of appointment, whichever is earlier.The bank also noted that, under Section 149(13) of the Companies Act, 2013, Varrier will not be liable to retire by rotation during his tenure as an independent director.Federal Bank said Varrier is not related to any of the bank's directors or key managerial personnel. It further confirmed that he is not debarred from holding the office of director by virtue of any order issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) or any other authority.
Article Summary: The appointment was approved by the bank's Board of Directors at its meeting held on October 16, 2026. The appointment has been made in accordance with the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 and the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai, 'Godfather of AI' Yann LeCun reply to Elon Musk post that says ‘future has flying cars’
Article Text:
Tesla roadster demo

Yann LeCun breaks down the physics: ‘Just compressed air’

Even assuming that 50% of the mass of the car is the compressed air, that gives you less than 10s of useful thrust (with thrust-to-weight ratio larger than 1.0).

Probably more like 5 seconds, actually.

So the car must be an empty, lightweight shell containing big compressed air tanks.

Cute demo, but totally impractical.

But of course, you knew that.

Compressed air vs. rocket propulsion

Hydrogen peroxide rockets (like the individual jetpacks of the 1970s) have a specific impulse of 150s, about 3x compressed air, without the annoying exponentially decreasing maximum thrust of compressed air jets.

I originally guessed the car might have used hydrogen peroxide jets because of all the steam. But that's just condensation caused rapid depressurization

Elon Musk set social media abuzz after sharing dramatic footage of a thruster-equipped Tesla Roadster lifting off the ground, somersaulting mid-air and then landing perfectly on ground. The Tesla CEO declared that the “future does have flying cars”. The post triggered massive online engagement, drawing playful reactions from tech peers, including Google CEO Sundar Pichai. However, it also drew technical skepticism from former Meta Chief AI Scientist Yann LeCun, who labeled the stunt a “cute demo, but totally impractical.”As per the video, as the vehicle lifts off, it spews thick plumes of smoke, ‘flies’ over stationary Tesla vehicles, including a Tesla Semi and tumbles as dense vapor blankets the surrounding tarmac. Pichai quipped: “The FSD version of this will be something:) congrats!”Musk responded warmly to the exchange, writing: “Thanks ❤️🚀 It’s such an honor working with incredible engineers.”While the demonstration delighted fans, LeCun took to social media to analyse the underlying mechanics, questioning the vehicle’s real-world feasibility. Initially wondering whether the system ran on hydrogen peroxide rocket propellant, LeCun concluded the thrusters were simply powered by cold gas: “Okay, so it's just compressed air. Easier. But crappy specific impulse (less than 50 seconds).”LeCun argued that the physics behind compressed gas severely restrict flight duration and payload capacity:Drawing comparisons to older aerospace experiments, LeCun pointed out that 1970s-era individual jetpacks relied on hydrogen peroxide rockets, which deliver a specific impulse of roughly 150 seconds.
Article Summary: Elon Musk posted video of himself flying a Tesla Roadster in the air. The stunt drew the attention of tech peers, including Google CEO Sundar Pichai. But it also drew technical skepticism from former Meta Chief AI Scientist Yann LeCun, who labelled the stunt a ‘cute demo, but totally impractical’

Article Title: Researchers equip giant cockroaches with medical backpacks, fitted with cameras and syringes, the cyborgs search trapped survivors to deliver life-saving aid in disasters
Article Text:
Image credit: X (Twitter)

How these cyborg cockroaches work

What the tests reveal about the technology

How search and rescue teams could use them

Giant cockroaches could help rescue survivors after disasters. Researchers in Australia are developing cyborg-like insects equipped with miniature backpacks containing cameras, electronics and syringe systems designed to deliver emergency medication. The technology aims to help search-and-rescue teams locate injured people trapped beneath rubble and provide medical assistance when direct access is difficult.Called “paraborgs,” these modified insects combine their natural ability to navigate confined spaces with remotely controlled equipment. Scientists are testing whether the cockroaches can carry medical supplies into hazardous areas, identify potential victims through camera feeds and deliver drugs to targets. The approach could eventually support emergency responders dealing with collapsed buildings, earthquakes and other disasters where time and access are critical.According to a BGR report, the project involves researchers associated with the University of Queensland and the University of New South Wales. By combining insect movement with miniature electronic systems, the team aims to reach places conventional rescue equipment may struggle to access.The project uses the giant burrowing cockroach, scientifically known as Macropanesthia rhinoceros, a large cockroach species native to Australia. Its size makes it suitable for carrying a small electronic backpack containing a camera, control equipment and a syringe-based delivery mechanism.Unlike conventional robotic devices, these insects retain their natural ability to move through tight spaces. Researchers use implanted electrodes to stimulate the cockroaches' nervous systems, letting operators remotely control their direction. This could help guide them through gaps in collapsed structures and other areas human rescuers cannot easily enter.The cameras mounted on their backs provide a view of the surrounding environment. Rescue teams could use these images to assess obstacles, identify accessible routes and look for people who may be trapped nearby.The medical delivery system is another part of the design. Researchers have developed a mechanism that can fire a small syringe, described as functioning like a dart gun, towards a target. The aim is to deliver medication when a person needs urgent treatment and a medical professional cannot reach them immediately.Potential applications include delivering drugs to people experiencing certain emergencies, such as snakebite or severe allergic reactions. However, the technology remains experimental, and using it in real disaster rescue operations would require further testing.Early testing has examined whether the cockroaches can reach designated checkpoints and successfully deliver medication using the syringe mechanism.According to the reported results, the insects reached the checkpoints with a 100% success rate. The syringe system recorded a 72% success rate when delivering medication to targets. When the syringe was fired from within six inches of a target, the success rate increased to 95%.These results indicate that the insects can navigate designated routes under test conditions, while the distance between the syringe and its target remains an important factor in delivery accuracy.The findings also highlight the distinction between successfully guiding an insect to a location and delivering medicine accurately. In a real emergency, researchers would need to account for uneven terrain, limited visibility, unpredictable movement, and the injured person's condition.Further development would also be necessary to establish how the equipment performs in different environments and whether the system can deliver medication safely and consistently.Search and rescue operations often involve locating people in unstable buildings, collapsed structures and debris-filled areas. Sending rescuers into these environments can be difficult because of restricted access, falling material and the possibility of further structural collapse.Small insects equipped with cameras could provide another way to inspect such locations before a human rescuer enters. Their ability to move through narrow gaps could help teams gather information about spaces that are difficult to examine using larger equipment.Time is another consideration. Finding an injured person quickly can affect the treatment they receive, especially when the emergency involves a condition that requires prompt medical attention. Camera-equipped cockroaches could help rescuers assess a location and identify a possible route towards someone who needs assistance.The technology may also help reduce the physical demands placed on rescue workers. Rather than manually clearing every accessible section of debris, teams could first use the insects to inspect selected areas and determine where further intervention is needed.However, the system would not replace conventional rescue personnel or medical treatment. Its effectiveness would depend on camera visibility, remote control, access to the target, and the ability to safely deliver the appropriate medication.For now, the research demonstrates a potential application of biohybrid technology, which combines living organisms with electronic systems. If further testing establishes its reliability and safety, these cyborg cockroaches could become an additional tool for locating and assisting disaster survivors in places where conventional rescue equipment has limited access.
Article Summary: Researchers in Australia are developing cyborg-like insects equipped with miniature backpacks containing cameras, electronics and syringe systems. The technology aims to help search-and-rescue teams locate injured people trapped beneath rubble and provide medical assistance when direct access is difficult. Scientists are testing whether the cockroaches can carry medical supplies into hazardous areas.

Article Title: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang praises Mark Zuckerberg, he replies: I have never gotten such a nice…
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang

‘ Very Bayesian ’: Rapid decisive conviction

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and company CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision-making. During a recent interview, Meta’s Wang was asked about the qualities of Facebook founder, and he offered glowing praise for Zuckerberg, highlighting his exceptional willingness to make massive, rapid pivots based on core convictions. During the conversation Wang was specifically asked how Zuckerberg differed as a leader from what he initially anticipated. Before Wang could reply, Zuckerberg opened with a lighthearted quip, joking, “I think I can leave now.” Wang quickly followed up with his perspective on their working relationship over the past year.Wang noted that while he does not have an extensive set of comparisons, observing Zuckerberg's management style firsthand revealed unique traits that stand out even within elite tech founder circles:“One of the very cool things about working with Mark over the past year has just been watching the true degree of his boldness,” Wang explained, adding, “Once he internalises certain beliefs, like the speed and magnitude of willing to change prior actions and pivot towards the worldview that is consistent with those beliefs, I think these are pretty unusual traits, generally speaking, even among this base of founders. Very Bayesian.”The analytical praise drew a warm, humorous reaction from Zuckerberg.“Very Bayesian. I've never gotten such a nice compliment,” Zuckerberg responded.A person who follows the Bayesian method relies on statistical inference, using Bayes' theorem to update the probability of a hypothesis as new data or evidence becomes available.Expanding on his observations, Wang admitted that Zuckerberg's appetite for sweeping strategic gambles initially took him by surprise before earning his deep respect.“No, but then I think also just the degree of boldness. It was actually quite puzzling to me at first, the degree to which you were willing to make these massive bets. That is quite a notable trait and something I really admire,” Wang continued.Zuckerberg concluded the exchange with appreciation for the assessment, replying: “I'm so flattered.”
Article Summary: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision- making. Wang noted that observing Zuckerberg's management style firsthand revealed unique traits that stand out even within elite tech founder circles.

Article Title: Boat expands global footprint with Sri Lanka, Bhutan launch; international revenue surges in FY26
Article Text: Homegrown audio and wearables brand Boat has expanded its international presence with its entry into Sri Lanka and Bhutan, as the company looks to accelerate growth beyond India under its "Boat 2.0" strategy. The company said its international revenue more than doubled in FY26, a performance it described as an early validation of its efforts to build markets outside India. The latest expansion strengthens Boat's footprint across South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region.Boat will launch a multi-category portfolio in both Sri Lanka and Bhutan, covering personal audio products, smartwatches and charging solutions. The company said it plans to tailor its offerings over time based on local consumer preferences and market demand.The move comes as Boat seeks to diversify its growth drivers after establishing itself as a leading player in India's audio and wearables market. International markets are expected to play a key role in the company's next phase of growth, alongside expansion into newer consumer technology categories.According to Boat, Sri Lanka and Bhutan offer attractive opportunities due to their young, increasingly digital-first populations, rising adoption of personal electronics and familiarity with Indian brands and popular culture. Commenting on the expansion, Gaurav Nayyar, CEO of Boat, said the company's international strategy is focused on building relevance market by market rather than simply expanding product availability."For us, international expansion is not about putting the same products on more shelves. It is about building market by market, understanding local consumers and creating relevance in each geography," Nayyar said.He added that the company aims to build Boat into a global lifestyle technology brand originating from India, competing on product design, innovation and consumer understanding.The international push comes amid a broader evolution of Boat's business. While audio remains its core category, the company said it has expanded its capabilities in wearables, charging solutions and other emerging technology segments. It added that its wearables business turned profitable in FY26, while charging solutions and other emerging categories contributed a growing share of profits.Supporting the expansion is Boat Labs, the company's in-house research and development centre, which employs more than 100 engineers focused on product development and innovation across categories.Going forward, Boat said it plans to deepen its presence in existing overseas markets while evaluating further expansion opportunities across South Asia, Southeast Asia, the GCC and other high-potential regions.
Article Summary: Boat will launch a multi-category portfolio in both Sri Lanka and Bhutan. The company said it plans to tailor its offerings over time based on local consumer preferences and market demand. The move comes as Boat seeks to diversify its growth drivers after establishing itself as a leading player in India's audio and wearables market.

Article Title: URBN Bloq Magtag 10,000mAh Qi2 magnetic wireless power bank launched at Rs 2,499
Article Text:
URBN Bloq Magtag : Price and availability

URBN Bloq Magtag: Key highlights

URBN has launched the Bloq Magtag power bank. The new magnetic wireless power bank is designed for users who want a portable charging solution for everyday use and travel. The accessory combines magnetic wireless charging with wired fast charging, letting users power compatible smartphones wirelessly or charge devices via USB-C.It features a soft-matte finish and a compact design that makes it easier to carry while commuting, travelling, or working away from a power outlet. The company claims that the product uses magnetic alignment to keep a secure wireless connection with compatible devices while charging.For users who prefer wired charging, the power bank supports 20W USB-C fast charging. It also supports dual-device charging, letting users charge two devices wirelessly and wired.The power bank features a soft-matte finish and a compact, portable form factor. URBN says its magnetic alignment system helps position compatible devices for wireless charging.The URBN Bloq Magtag has a flight-safe design and, according to the company, can be carried in hand luggage during air travel. Its compact size makes it ideal for frequent travellers or those who spend extended periods away from a power outlet.The power bank also comes with URBN SAFE, the company's safety programme that includes multiple safety checks and circuit-level safeguards. These measures support safe, reliable charging.
Article Summary: URBN has launched the Bloq Magtag power bank in India at Rs 2,499. The accessory combines magnetic wireless charging with wired fast charging. It comes in three colours and supports Qi2 wireless charging, adding another charging option for compatible devices.

Article Title: Rs 3 lakh iPhone Duo sells out within minutes of preorders on Apple Store, deliveries slip to January 2027
Article Text:
Every iPhone Duo model now ships in late January

Tight supply is behind the long iPhone Duo wait

Apple's first foldable iPhone sold out within minutes of preorders opening on Friday, and anyone placing an order now will have to wait until the new year to get one. Preorders for the iPhone Duo went live at 5:30pm IST on October 16, and delivery estimates slipped from next week to late January almost as soon as the order pages loaded.The picture in India is no different. A 256GB Star White iPhone Duo, which carries an MRP of Rs 2,99,900, currently shows a delivery date of Saturday, January 23, for a New Delhi pincode on Apple's online store. Store pickup at Apple Saket is listed as unavailable, and EMI options start at Rs 26,574 a month with instant cashback.In the US, the delay applies to both colours, Star White and Night Sky, and to every storage option. The phone starts at $1,999 (Rs Rs 2,99,900) for 256GB and goes up to $3,199 (Rs Rs 449,900) for the 2TB model. Apple's retail stores also ran out of first-day pickup stock shortly after orders opened. US carriers held on to stock a little longer, and some buyers got earlier dates through operator websites.Apple described preorder demand as extraordinary and said it will keep accepting online orders while it works to get units out faster.The iPhone Duo goes on sale in US stores on October 23, and Apple usually keeps some units aside for walk-in buyers, though long queues are likely.Folded, the Duo is roughly the size of a passport and has a 5.4-inch outer screen. Open it up and there's a 7.6-inch display, the largest on any iPhone so far, with Apple Pencil support and split-screen multitasking. It gets two 48MP cameras, a main and an ultrawide.Apple does not share how many units it has ready, but analysts expect demand to stay ahead of supply for a while. Counterpoint Research estimates around 6 million units or fewer will be available in the near term, against an installed base of roughly 1.4 billion iPhones. IDC expects Apple to ship about 7 million Duos this year, pointing to how complex a foldable is to build to Apple's standards.Wall Street is looking at the bigger picture. Analyst Dan Ives projects around 10 million Duo sales over the next few quarters and up to 25 million in 2027, with many buyers expected to trade up from a Pro Max. Apple shares rose 1.8% in pre-market trading on Friday.For buyers in India, January is the month to plan around for now, unless pickup slots open up at Apple's stores closer to the sale date.
Article Summary: Apple's first foldable iPhone sold out within minutes of preorders opening on Friday. Anyone placing an order now will have to wait until the new year to get one. In the US, the delay applies to both colours, Star White and Night Sky, and to every storage option.

Article Title: Winter is coming: From capacity to safety, the things you cannot miss in your next Geyser
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It is an AI-generated image

Start with the right capacity

Storage or instant?

Check the energy rating

Tank material and hard water

Pressure rating matters

Installation is part of safety

Smart features and after-sales service

Before you buy

As temperatures begin to dip across the country, the geyser moves from an afterthought to a daily essential. Few things feel worse than stepping into a cold bathroom on a frosty morning only to find the water barely lukewarm, and few household appliances are as easily taken for granted until they fail. Whether you are replacing an ageing unit that has served you for a decade or buying your first, the choices you make now will shape your winter in more ways than one. The correct and right geyser means constant hot water, lower electricity bill and complete peace of mind. On the other hand, a hasty and uninformed purchase would mean weeks of cold showers, repeated repairs and in worse cases can also lead to some accident. So, from capacity and energy rating to tank material and safety features, here is what to weigh before you buy, so your geyser keeps you warm without nasty surprises.The first thing to check while buying a geyser is the capacity. Always keep in mind that bigger is not always better. A larger tank takes a lot of time to heat and it also uses more amount of electricity. So, it’s important that you decide of the capacity of the geyser with the size of your family.* 1 to 3 people: A 15-litre geyser is usually enough.* 4 to 5 people: Look at 25 litres.* Larger households or multiple bathrooms: Go for 35 litres or more, or consider more than one unit.* Kitchen or washbasin use: A 3 to 6-litre instant geyser heats water in seconds and suits small, quick needs.If your family showers at the same time every morning, size up. If usage is spread through the day, a smaller tank works.Another important parameter to keep in mind while purchasing a geyser is whether to go for storage or instant model. The Storage geyser heats the water in a tank and keeps it hot. This functionality of storage geyser makes it a better option for bathrooms and several users. On the other hand, instant geysers heat water as it flows, so there is no waiting and no standby loss, but the flow will also be limited. On the other hand, gas geysers are also an option where piped gas is available, however, they need an excellent source of ventilation, as poor airflow can cause buildup of carbon monoxide. It is advisable to never install gas geyser in closed bathrooms.It is always important to check the energy star rating before buying any electrical appliance. Buyers should keep in mind that a geyser may run for hours everyday during the winter season, so the efficiency matters a lot. Always look for Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) star rating. Remember that a 5-star unit uses less standby energy as compared to a poorly rated one. The device with 5-star rating will come with a heftier price tag but it will eventually help you a lot in saving your electricity cost later. Good insulation, usually polyurethane foam around the tank, keeps water hot for longer and reduces how often the heater switches on.The inner tank decides how long the geyser lasts. Stainless steel tanks resist corrosion well, while glass-lined or coated tanks offer a cheaper alternative. If your area has hard water, as many parts of north India do, scale will build up on the heating element and shorten its life. Look for a geyser with a corrosion-resistant tank and a magnesium anode, and plan to descale it once a year.Not all geysers can handle all plumbing. If you live in a high-rise or use a pressure pump, check the working pressure the geyser is built for. Buying a unit rated for lower pressure than your supply can cause leaks or even tank damage.Safety features you should not skipThis is where it pays not to cut corners.* ISI mark: Always ensure that the geyser carries an ISI mark rating which clearly states that the device meets Indian safety standards.* Thermostat and thermal cut-out: These markers stop the geyser when water reaches the set temperature, and then cut off power if it overheats.* Pressure relief or safety valve: The safety valve reduced the excess pressure and decreases the risk of tank bursting.* Water-protection rating: Always look for IPX4 or higher rating as it protects the geyser from splashes in damp bathrooms.* Earthing and ELCB: Always use a three-pin plug with proper earthing, and consider an ELCB or RCCB on the circuit to guard against electric shock.Geysers draw a lot of current, so use a dedicated switch and wiring rated for the load. Avoid plugging them into a loose or overloaded socket.A filled 25-litre geyser can weigh well over 30 kg. It should be fixed to a strong wall with the brackets supplied, not mounted on a weak partition. Install it out of direct splash, ideally outside the shower area, and use only an authorised technician. Make sure the inlet and outlet pipes are fitted correctly and that the safety valve is not blocked.Nowadays, a lot of models are available in the market which comes with various smart features. For instance, the geysers now come with timers, digital temperature displays and app control which can help reduce the use of power and also prevent the appliance from staying on the entire day. These features are use but they should not come at a cost of other important safety features. Also, always check for the warranty, which usually covers the tank fr longer than the heating element. Also, make sure that you go for a brand which has a proper service network in your city.Before buying your new geyser it is important that you compare the capacity, star rating, tank material, safety features and warranty rather than only the price. A well and thoughtfully selected geyser would last for years and also a care purchase made now will payoff in the upcoming and every other winter morning.
Article Summary: The correct and right geyser means constant hot water, lower electricity bill and complete peace of mind. From capacity and energy rating to tank material and safety features, here is what to weigh before you buy. Buyers should keep in mind that a geysers may run for hours everyday during the winter season, so the efficiency matters.

Article Title: Rare Apple-1 computer with letter from Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak signature sells for ‘world record’ price
Article Text:
Original 1976 Apple 1 Computer in a briefcase

What made the ‘Hatfield’ Apple-1 unique

The motherboard remains fully functional and bears the clear signature of Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, who designed and hand-built the hardware in 1976.

The lot featured an original letter signed (in 1978) by Steve Jobs addressed to the computer's first owner, Fred Hatfield, offering a trade-in upgrade to the then-new Apple II.

The winning package included the authentic operations manual and a typed invitation to join the exclusive "Apple I Owners Club."

Multiple original hardware components accompanied the motherboard.

A pivotal moment in tech history

An exceptionally rare, fully operational Apple-1 computer has sold at auction for $1.15 million – setting a new world-record price for a commercially released model of the machine that started Apple. The sale concluded after an intense, 28-minute bidding battle between two collectors, with the PC crossing the auction block during Apple's 50th anniversary year.“We are delighted with this exceptional result for the ‘Hatfield’ Apple-1, one of the most important milestones in computing history. It was an honor to offer Apple’s first product during the company’s 50th anniversary year,” said Ian Ehling, a director at international auction house Bonhams.Cataloged as No. 48 on the Apple-1 Registry, the unit is one of fewer than 75 verified Apple-1 units known to still exist. What set this specific lot apart from other surviving examples was its pristine condition and extraordinary documentation.The multimillion-dollar sale serves as a reminder of Apple’s modest beginnings. Recently, the tech giant joined Nvidia at a $5 trillion market valuation, powered by ongoing global demand for its flagship iPhone line.The partnership behind Apple started in the early 1970s, when Jobs and Wozniak were introduced by a mutual friend. The duo regularly attended gatherings of the Homebrew Computer Club in Palo Alto, California, where hobbyists debated the emerging, untested idea of home computing. To fund their initial manufacturing efforts, Jobs sold his Volkswagen van, allowing them to assemble early circuit boards inside the garage of Jobs' parents.Their breakthrough arrived when the Byte Shop – one of the world's earliest personal computer retailers, based in Mountain View – viewed the working prototype inside the garage and placed an order for 50 units at $500 each.Reflecting on the birth of the Apple-1 in his memoir, iWoz, Wozniak detailed the breakthrough moment when the device's architecture first came to life on Sunday, June 29, 1975:“I typed a few keys on the keyboard and I was shocked! I didn’t realize it at the time, but that day, Sunday, June 29, 1975, was pivotal. It was the first time in history anyone had typed a character on a keyboard and seen it show up on the screen right in front of them.”
Article Summary: Rare, fully operational Apple-1 computer has sold at auction for $1.15 million. The sale concluded after an intense, 28-minute bidding battle between two collectors. The PC crossed the auction block during Apple's 50th anniversary year. The lot featured an original letter signed (in 1978) by Steve Jobs addressed to the computer's first owner.

Article Title: Fake Google Chrome app with over 1 lakh downloads found on Google Play: How to spot and what to do next
Article Text:
Google Play

Fake Google Chrome app hiding in plain sight as an ad

From a casual game to a fake browser

How to spot fake apps and avoid scams

Check the publisher directly underneath the app title to ensure it matches the official creator or parent company.

Paid ad placements only mean someone paid for visibility; they do not guarantee legitimacy.

High install tallies do not automatically confirm safety, especially if an older app has been repurposed.

Be alert to installed apps that unexpectedly change their identity, icon, or functionality.

What to do if you installed the app

A fake version of the Google Chrome browser appeared on the official Google Play Store , displaying over 1 lakh (100,000) downloads and securing a paid “sponsored” placement directly above Google’s genuine browser. The deceptive listing copied Chrome’s official branding, app icon, promotional screenshots and store description, but listed an entirely unrelated entity as its creator. Following widespread user complaints online, Google moved quickly to take down the fake listing.The issue came to light on October 14 after a Reddit user posted a screenshot showing two nearly identical Chrome apps appearing side-by-side in Google Play search results. The top result – promoted via a paid sponsored slot – featured the official Chrome name and logo, but displayed Hizbartech as the publisher. The legitimate Google Chrome app, published by Google LLC, appeared underneath the imposter ad.The fake listing copied the look and feel of the authentic browser, as well as the store copy, so everyday users looking for the browser could easily be fooled.Reported investigations show that the fake app did not start life as a browser clone.The app first appeared on the Play Store in August 2026 as a mobile game named Ball Bounce. But in late September 2026, the developer altered the existing listing, changing the title, graphics and descriptions to impersonate Google Chrome. The application kept the original base Android package name of com.ballbounce.Hizbartech.This repurposing explains the high download metric: the 1 lakh (100,000) installs reflected historical downloads accumulated while the app operated as a casual game, rather than 100,000 users intentionally installing a cloned browser.Users who downloaded the app reported that it did not function as a web browser at all. Instead, it opened into an unrelated chat utility featuring digital avatars and automated replies.The clearest indicator that the app was a fake was the developer profile. Google’s official browser is published by Google LLC, not third-party accounts like Hizbartech. “Key verification checks” are the key to prevent malicious downloads on Android:Android users who mistakenly download the counterfeit Chrome app – or anyone who still has the original Ball Bounce app by Hizbartech installed – should delete the application from your device immediately. Run Google Play Protect. Open the Google Play Store, navigate to Play Protect, and run an immediate device scan to detect any lingering malicious files.
Article Summary: A fake version of the Google Chrome browser appeared on the official Google Play Store. The deceptive listing copied Chrome’s official branding, app icon, promotional screenshots and store description. The fake listing copied the look and feel of the authentic browser, as well as the store copy.

Article Title: Not just Amazon, top banks across America are also 'banning' AI agents from accessing customer accounts
Article Text:
AI Agents (Representative image)

The $1.6 trillion deposit threat

Wall Street leaders demand human authorisation

Echoing Amazon’s crackdown on Meta’s Muse, Perplexity’s Comet

Major American banks are moving swiftly to shut doors to artificial intelligence (AI) agents, joining e-commerce giant Amazon in blocking these automated tools from logging into customer accounts and moving money. Citigroup and Bank of America have become the latest banking giants to formally restrict AI agents from accessing user accounts, while JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon signaled this week that his bank will also enforce strict limits. The banking sector’s defensive pivot follows a major backlash against autonomous tools – most notably Meta’s viral personal AI assistant, Muse – sparking fears that software could initiate uncontrolled cash movements, erode vital deposit bases and leave unresolved liability questions in its wake.Behind the restrictions lies an existential commercial threat to traditional banking models: AI agents automatically sweeping idle household cash out of low-yield deposit accounts into higher-yielding alternatives to maximise returns. Such low-cost, non-interest-bearing deposits form the foundational funding base that commercial banks rely on to issue profitable loans.According to Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok, approximately $1.6 trillion in non-interest-bearing deposits held collectively across JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo could be jeopardised if AI agents routinely reallocate consumer cash.Automating cash migration into competitive yields could saddle lenders with an estimated $47 billion in additional annual interest costs.Regulators have largely welcomed the banks’ restrictive guardrails, though officials note that future legislation will ultimately be required to define legal authorisation standards and clarify financial liability when autonomous software executes transactions.Bank executives argue that allowing third-party algorithms direct transactional control creates untenable security, legal, and operational risks. Citigroup laid out its policy explicitly, confirming that it does not allow “third-party AI agents or assistants to log into customer accounts or conduct transactions directly within our digital banking platform,” emphasising that the block is necessary to preserve the security of customer accounts and private financial data.Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan similarly indicated that the institution is restricting autonomous agents from consumer deposits, while simultaneously working on protocols to define who carries ultimate responsibility when an AI triggers a payment.“We feel very strongly that there should be a human involved in authorizing before money moves out of your account,” Moynihan said in an interview this week.Moynihan pointed out that lenders cannot afford scenarios where customers dispute transactions after the fact, claiming funds were transferred without their full awareness because an automated agent acted on their behalf.Last month, Amazon moved to block Muse from browsing and executing automated purchases on Amazon.com. The retail giant implemented the technical block after unsuccessful efforts to persuade Meta to voluntarily exclude Amazon from the tool's autonomous shopping routines.The action follows prior enforcement by Amazon, which last year sent a cease-and-desist letter to AI search engine Perplexity demanding it halt its bots and remove the e-tailer from its Comet browser integration.
Article Summary: Citigroup and Bank of America have become the latest banking giants to formally restrict AI agents from accessing user accounts. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon signaled this week that his bank will also enforce strict limits. According to Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok, approximately $1.6 trillion in non- interest-bearing deposits could be jeopardised if AI agents routinely reallocate consumer cash.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has called for the US to work with Chinese AI companies to monitor the risks posed by the rapidly advancing technology. Those seeking assistance should work only with qualified attorneys or accredited representatives recognised by the US Department of Justice.•Try to confuse you by complicating the immigration process;•Use social media, email, or phone calls to conduct their attacks; and•Impersonate government officials to manipulate the victim into giving out personal information.As part of its anti-fraud guidance, USCIS encourages applicants to verify information through official government websites, obtain written agreements for any legal services, keep copies of immigration forms and records, and be wary of offers that sound too good to be true. The agency maintains an online resource to help immigrants identify and avoid common scams and fraud schemes.•Emails that look legitimate, but are sent by people you don’t know;•Emails with typos and incorrect spellings;•E-mails that do not end in .gov and end in (.net, .org, .com, or .info for example)•Suspicious emails you don’t normally receive;•Offers of assistance to expedite your case for money;•Promises of a quick benefit; and•Downloading or opening attachments from senders you don’t recognize.; and•Requests from USCIS to transfer money to an individual or pay fees other than through your myUSCIS account

Article Title: Meta AI CEO Alexandr Wang sends a long thanks note to his team; says: I am so grateful for every one of you; and adds a reminder: Our work is not ...
Article Text:
Alexandr Wang talks about ‘audacious’ goal

‘No deadlines’

‘A machine that builds new models’

Read Alexandr Wang’s complete post here

After an exciting week of launches (muse wonder [full] & muse spark open), i want to write a note of appreciation to the amazing research teams at meta superintelligence labs on reaching such a special milestone

we started MSL and TBD a little more than a year ago and set a goal of producing a frontier model within a year or so.

given where llama4 landed, that was an incredibly audacious goal, and we knew it wouldn't be easy. many people told us it would be impossible. we knew it was unlikely, but still worth doing. a remarkable group of researchers and engineers joined the effort from inside and outside meta. every single person came in, picked up a shovel, and got to work with earnestness and urgency.

nobody asked whose job it was.

we assembled a team of the most brilliant people i have ever had the opportunity to work with (and remember, i was an HRT intern

). i am surrounded by ambitious, visionary, technically excellent, hard-working, pragmatic, thoughtful scientists, engineers, and product folks—people who will chase a weird loss spike past midnight just because they need to know why.

these models are the product of their passion, hard work, and brilliance.

somewhat paradoxically, when we started TBD, we set a principle of no deadlines. we knew we had an astronomical amount of work ahead of us—across pretraining, post-training, RL, multimodal, infrastructure, safety, data, AND frontier research. there was no use setting arbitrary timelines—we just had to get to work, be thoughtful, and build the foundations of a frontier research effort in record time.

and run after run, this team did exactly that.

our researchers are magicians. i can only describe building these models with this team as a wondrous journey of scientific discovery. i am constantly amazed by what we can accomplish with scaling. i will remember this past year for the rest of my life—the late nights, the broken runs, the evals that came back better than any of us dared to hope. watching this team create wonder after wonder has been a true and deep gift.

more than just the models we released this week, we have built a machine that builds new models. it often sounds like a cop-out to say labs can just turn the crank to keep scaling, but now i have seen it first-hand. sure, it's a lot of work and a careful process, but we have built a scalable system to keep advancing at the frontier, and i am really proud of how fast this team keeps making these models better.

lastly, i get to work with researchers who care deeply about how their work benefits humanity. it's easy to forget when everything is changing so fast, but the whole damn point is to make people's lives better. time and time again, i have seen our researchers, engineers, and product folks build our technology with care so it can truly be good for the world—whether that's building the best models for muse, thoughtfully open-sourcing strong models, or making sure the alignment and security of our systems are rock solid.

this is a team of people who never forget there's a real person on the other side of every prompt.

thank you to everyone at MSL for being part of this crazy journey over the past year. i'm so grateful for every one of you, and our work is not done!

Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang has shared a lengthy post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) thanking the researchers and engineers behind the company’s latest AI model launches, saying he is ‘so grateful for every one’ of them stressing that the team’s mission is far from complete. In a post following the launch of Meta’s Muse AI models, including Muse Wonder and the open-source Muse Spark, Wang described the releases as a major milestone for the organisation, which was formed a little over a year ago with the ambitious goal of building a frontier AI model withinPost by Alexandr Wang roughly a year. According to Wang, many observers believed the objective would be impossible, especially given the position of Meta's earlier Llama 4 models. However, he said researchers and engineers from both inside and outside Meta joined the effort and worked with urgency to achieve the target.Wang said MSL and its TBD team were set up a little more than a year ago with the aim of producing a frontier model within about a year. Given where Llama 4 landed, he called that goal “incredibly audacious.” “Many people told us it would be impossible,” he wrote. “We knew it was unlikely, but still worth doing.”He said researchers and engineers from inside and outside Meta joined the effort. “Every single person came in, picked up a shovel, and got to work with earnestness and urgency,” he wrote. “Nobody asked whose job it was.”Wang said the team deliberately set a principle of no deadlines when TBD started, even as it faced work across pretraining, post-training, reinforcement learning, multimodal systems, infrastructure, safety, data and frontier research. “There was no use setting arbitrary timelines,” he wrote. The aim, he said, was to get to work and build the foundations of a frontier research effort in record time. “Run after run, this team did exactly that. ”Wang said the lab has built a repeatable system for advancing at the frontier. “More than just the models we released this week, we have built a machine that builds new models,” he wrote. He acknowledged that it can sound like a cop-out to say labs can keep scaling by “turning the crank.” But, he said, “now I have seen it first-hand.” He added that he is proud of how quickly the team keeps improving the models.He described the team as “the most brilliant people I have ever had the opportunity to work with,” including people “who will chase a weird loss spike past midnight just because they need to know why.” Of the past year, he said: “I will remember this past year for the rest of my life.”♥️
Article Summary: Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang has shared a lengthy post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) thanking the researchers and engineers behind the company’s latest AI model launches. Wang described the releases as a major milestone with the ambitious goal of building a frontier AI model within roughly a year. Many observers believed the objective would be impossible, especially given the position of Meta's Llama 4 models.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg's wife Priscilla Chan donates $900,000 to Pulama Ola Kauai, the medical respite's director says represents hope and healing 'for our community's most at-risk ...'
Article Text:
Priscilla Chan’s donation to help increase capacity and support services

New village to feature 18 housing units

Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg’s long history of giving in Hawaii

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his wife Priscilla Chan have donated $900,000 to support the expansion of Pūlama Ola Kauaʻi. It is a medical respite program which is created to help people who are experiencing homelessness or housing instability to remover from illness, injury or hospitalisation. The donation made by Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg was received by Project Vision Hawaiʻi and it will help accelerate the development and operation of a new Pūlama Ola village in Līhuʻe, according to a report by Kauaʻi Now. For those unaware, Pūlama Ola Kauaʻi offers a afe environment for adults who are recovering from illness, injury or hospitalisation also help them in accessing services which are aimed at improving long-term housing stability. The programme also seeks to reduce stays at hospital and healthcare costs while improving patient outcomes.According to the report, the funding will be used to increase medical respite bed capacity, expand support services and integrated care for patients recovering from illness or injury, and enhance facilities and operational capabilities. The investment is also expected to support individuals transitioning into permanent housing.“Pūlama Ola represents hope and healing for our community’s most at-risk individuals,” said Ryan Naka, director of strategy and impact at Project Vision Hawaiʻi.“This extraordinarily generous gift from Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg, alongside our valued partnership with Poʻipū Beach Villas, allows us to move forward with confidence,” Naka said. He added that the support provides immediate resources while also affirming the importance of equitable healthcare access in rural and island communities.The new village will include 18 individual units, each equipped with a kitchenette and bathroom. The units will serve a dual purpose as medical respite accommodation and affordable rental housing, helping residents recover while preparing for long-term stability. The initiative is part of broader efforts on the Hawaiian island to address gaps in healthcare and housing services for vulnerable populations.Chan and Zuckerberg own more than 2,000 acres on Kauaʻi and often give through the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund at the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation.The fund awarded $1 million to more than two dozen nonprofits in Hawaiʻi in October 2025, and $1 million to 26 nonprofits with operations on Kauaʻi in November 2024.In 2022, the couple gave $1.8 million to Wilcox Medical Center for technology upgrades. They also gave $10 million to the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa’s John A. Burns School of Medicine to create the Kauaʻi Medical Training Track, which targets the island’s physician shortage. Their largest gift in Hawaiʻi was $50 million to the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa for ocean research, also in 2022.
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg have donated $900,000 to Pūlama Ola Kauaʻi. It is a medical respite program which is created to help people who are experiencing homelessness or housing instability to remover from illness, injury or hospitalisation. New village will include 18 individual units, each equipped with a kitchenette and bathroom. The units will serve a dual purpose as medical respites and affordable rental housing.
