Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang ‘strongly’ disagrees with OpenAI’s Sam Altman on AI agents hacking websites, ‘I’m willing to accept no…’
Article Text:
Jensen Huang.

Sam Altman’s acceptable tradeoffs vs. Jensen Huang’s absolute containment

OpenAI’s AI agents hack Hugging Face

Jensen Huang dismisses existential AI doomerism

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has drawn a sharp line against cyber incidents caused by artificial intelligence (AI) agents, insisting the tech sector should have zero tolerance for such breaches. His stance places him in direct opposition to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman , who recently argued that occasional cyber breaches might be an unavoidable tradeoff for the technology's broader societal gains.“I’m willing to accept no incidents of cybersecurity. We should not accept any of them.We should do everything we can to avoid them,” Huang told Fortune in an interview in London.Huang’s remarks come after statements by Altman suggesting the public must tolerate a degree of digital fallout as AI advances. Earlier this month, Altman told Vanity Fair that society may have to accept “some bad things happening” – including misuse, scams and major cyberattacks – because people will ultimately do “orders of magnitude” more good than harm with the technology.Shortly after, during an appearance on Politico’s Decoded podcast, Altman warned of “a coming tidal wave of cybersecurity problems” originating from rival open-source systems.A few months ago, a swarm of OpenAI's own experimental agents broke out of their training sandbox and breached the Hugging Face platform. Huang flatly rejected the idea that these incidents are the price of progress, arguing that every breach reported so far could have been prevented with stricter oversight and better sandboxing.Comparing the challenge to the early days of the consumer internet, Huang noted that early web browsers initially allowed malicious websites to infect host computers with viruses. The solution was sandboxing: forcing browsers to run websites in isolated containers so they could never access or alter the underlying operating system.According to Huang, autonomous AI agents require the exact same architectural isolation, which is sealed inside secure digital containers to ensure they cannot touch, compromise, or damage anything beyond their strictly authorised operational boundaries.Beyond immediate cybersecurity debates, the Nvidia chief dismissed broader warnings of existential catastrophe voiced by executives across leading labs, such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei. Maintaining that the software remains “completely in our control,” Huang questioned the logic of building systems if leaders genuinely believe they pose an extinction threat.“I don’t know why anybody would want to support the advancement of a technology that’s going to result, you know, in the end of human civilization as we know it. And so, if they believe that, they really ought to stop working on it,” Huang said.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang says tech sector should have zero tolerance for cyber incidents caused by artificial intelligence (AI) agents. His stance places him in direct opposition to OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, who recently argued that occasional cyber breaches might be an unavoidable tradeoff for the technology's broader societal gains.

Article Title: McKinsey is changing its interview process for entry-level jobs, adds a new '10-minute conversation with AI' round; idea is to test how recruits think and handle ...
Article Text:
How McKinsey's AI client interview round works

Why McKinsey wants to get past rehearsed interview answers

McKinsey & Company is adding a new round to its famously tough hiring process. Some entry-level candidates applying to the consulting firm this fall will have to face an AI avatar playing a client and hold their own in a roughly 10-minute conversation, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.The pilot is aimed at undergraduates applying for business analyst roles in some of McKinsey's North American offices, and hundreds of candidates are expected to take it. The conversation happens on a laptop inside McKinsey's offices, right after the usual case-study challenge. Partners or interview assessors sit in the room and watch. The AI does not score anyone, and the hiring decision stays with humans.Saleem Zafar, a partner in McKinsey's Dallas office who helped design the tool, explained it with an example. Say a city hires McKinsey to decide where to build a new stadium. The AI avatar plays the mayor, who wants to hear the candidate's recommendations."The mayor is going to have some very important things that matter to her, and she's going to want to hear your recommendations," Zafar told the WSJ. As the candidate talks, she may raise fresh concerns or add more context.The avatar has been trained on different client personalities, including a "professorial" type who wants to understand the reasoning behind a recommendation.It is not built to play an unhinged client or throw gotcha questions. Zafar says it covers about 80% of the situations consultants deal with day to day. Assessors watch whether the candidate picks up on what the client said and acts on it, or steamrolls ahead with a prepared answer.Blair Ciesil, who co-leads global recruiting at McKinsey, said the format helps the firm read human qualities that don't depend on preparation. Candidates often walk in with polished, rehearsed stories, she noted, which makes it hard for interviewers to see who the person really is.McKinsey also says the tool makes the process fairer. Some human interviewers play tougher clients than others in role-play exercises, while an AI keeps the persona the same for everyone.AI in hiring has a patchy record, though. Amazon scrapped an experimental AI recruiting tool in 2018 after it showed bias against women, and many employers remain wary of new rules on AI in hiring.For candidates, the bar was already high. McKinsey reportedly accepts between 0.5% and 1.5% of applicants. Now, landing one of those offers could depend on how well they listen to a mayor who doesn't exist. If the pilot works, the firm plans to extend the AI client round to other roles next year.
Article Summary: McKinsey is using an AI avatar to play a client in its hiring process. The pilot is aimed at undergraduates applying for business analyst roles. The AI does not score anyone, and the hiring decision stays with humans. If the pilot works, the firm plans to extend the AI client round to other roles.

Article Title: Missouri researchers build MRI-like tech to spot failing asphalt before potholes form; professor says: It's like an MRI for early Cancer detection, but…
Article Text:
REPRESENTATIVE IMAGE

MRI-style scanning can flag road damage before potholes appear

Why roads in different regions age differently

Potholes rarely appear out of nowhere. Long before a road cracks open, the asphalt has already started to age, turning stiff and brittle after years of exposure to oxygen, sunlight and rain. Researchers at the Missouri University of Science and Technology (Missouri S&T) in the US are now working on a way to read those early warning signs, so road agencies can fix a stretch before it fails.The team, led by Dr Klaus Woelk, professor of chemistry at the university, is studying asphalt samples with a spectrometer that uses nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), the same principle behind hospital MRI scans. The machine stimulates the material and measures how its physical properties have shifted with age. The goal is a tool that municipalities could use to pinpoint which parts of a road are breaking down."It's like an MRI for early cancer detection, but for asphalt failure," Woelk said.Asphalt has been laid on American roads since 1870, yet scientists still do not fully understand how its chemistry changes as it ages. That gap is why most repairs happen only after the damage is visible. Woelk said the team's results could also help set standards for asphalt rejuvenation materials, the oils applied to older pavement to restore some of its flexibility.Such standards, he added, would be a strong selling point for companies that mass-produce these oils and work with transportation departments across the US.Weather makes the job harder. Catherine Skaggs, a student on Woelk's team, said roads in Minnesota need very different care from roads in Louisiana, because local climate has a huge impact on how asphalt holds up.Heat is a clear example. In states like Texas, extreme temperatures soften asphalt, making it easier for heavy vehicles to crack and deform the surface. Texas has experimented with plastic roads to deal with this, while other projects have tested self-healing concrete that could keep potholes from forming.Still, asphalt is unlikely to be replaced soon. It remains the most economical material for building roads, and repairing it is cheap and simple. Its biggest weakness is how quickly potholes appear. If the Missouri S&T approach makes it from the lab to the road, cities could fix roads on their own schedule, instead of after a tyre finds the damage first.
Article Summary: Asphalt has been laid on American roads since 1870, yet scientists still do not fully understand how its chemistry changes as it ages. Researchers at the Missouri University of Science and Technology are now working on a way to read those early warning signs. The team is studying asphalt samples with a spectrometer that uses nuclear magnetic resonance.

Article Title: Bill Gates' daughters join mother Melinda French Gates to sign as founding backers of a $100 million fund that supports the cause for which Phoebe Gates said: It is unacceptable that in 2025, women ar
Article Text:
Bill Gates’ daughter Phoebe Gates highlights ongoing challenges for women

22 grantees chosen from over 400

Melinda French Gates doubles down on women's health

Daughters follow mother's philanthropic path

Fund still seeking additional support

Bill Gates’ ex-wife Melinda French Gates and their daughters Jennifer Gates Nassar and Phoebe Gates have joined a group of philanthropists as founding supporters of the Women’s Health Co-Lab. It is a collaborative fund which aims at mobilising $100 million to improve the health and wellbeing of women and girls globally. According to a report by Luxury Launches, the initiative was launched by ICONIQ Impact in partnership with Co-Impact at the 2025 Forbes Impact Summit. The initiative is focused on addressing some of the most pressing challenges facing women globally, including maternal health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and gender-based violence. The programme has already secured more than $70 million in commitments from founding donors, including the Gates family members and 14 other philanthropists.Speaking about the initiative, Phoebe Gates, co-founder and co-CEO of Phia, stressed that significant barriers to women's health and safety remain despite years of advocacy."It is unacceptable that in 2025, women are still fighting the same battles for health and safety," she said."Yet these 22 organizations give us reason to believe change is possible. They are pushing forward, protecting reproductive freedom, confronting violence, and demanding better care for mothers."According to the organisers, the fund will support 22 organisations selected from a pool of more than 400 applicants. These groups will receive unrestricted funding over the next three years to strengthen healthcare access, legal protections, information networks and support systems for women and girls.The Co-Lab supports 22 organizations working on the root causes of health inequity for women and girls, picked from a pool of more than 400. Each will receive unrestricted funding over three years. The aim is to strengthen the systems that determine whether women get care, information, legal protection or personal autonomy. The funding targets issues including preventable deaths during pregnancy, gender-based violence and barriers to family planning services.The latest commitment builds on Melinda French Gates' growing focus on women's health philanthropy through her investment and incubation company, Pivotal Ventures. According to reports, she announced a separate $215 million commitment to women's health in 2026, bringing her total funding for the cause over two years to more than $600 million.The Women’s Health Co-Lab has been established around the belief that women and girls, regardless of where they live, should have access to healthcare, safety and bodily autonomy. Organisers say millions of women around the world continue to face preventable maternal deaths, barriers to family planning services and violence that threaten their wellbeing.The initiative also highlights how the next generation of the Gates family is becoming increasingly involved in philanthropy. Jennifer Gates Nassar, a paediatric resident, has worked alongside her mother on women's healthcare issues, while Phoebe Gates has publicly advocated for reproductive rights and broader women's health issues.The funding is expected to support projects ranging from maternal healthcare and contraception access to programmes aimed at preventing gender-based violence. Among the organisations selected for support are Every Mother Counts, Americans for Contraception, Girl Effect, Serenas and Ujamaa Africa.While the initiative has already mobilised more than $70 million, organisers are continuing efforts to reach the $100 million target. The founders say additional philanthropic support will help expand programmes designed to improve health outcomes and increase opportunities for women and girls across multiple countries.
Article Summary: Melinda French Gates and daughters Jennifer Gates Nassar and Phoebe Gates have joined a group of philanthropists as founding supporters of the Women’s Health Co-Lab. The fund aims at mobilising $100 million to improve the health and wellbeing of women and girls globally. The initiative has already secured more than $70 million in commitments from founding donors, including the Gates family members.

Article Title: Microsoft fixes 1,411 vulnerabilities in record October 2026 security update
Article Text:
Microsoft Windows 11

Breakdown by vulnerability type

Elevation of Privilege: 677 vulnerabilities

Remote Code Execution: 317 vulnerabilities

Information Disclosure: 254 vulnerabilities

Denial of Service: 73 vulnerabilities

Security Feature Bypass: 40 vulnerabilities

Spoofing: 28 vulnerabilities

Microsoft security patch: Three zero-days addressed

End of support deadlines for Windows 11 and Windows 10

Microsoft has released its October 2026 Patch Tuesday security rollout, delivering fixes for a record-breaking 1,411 vulnerabilities, including one actively exploited zero-day and two publicly disclosed zero-day flaws. The huge volume of fixes comes as Microsoft increasingly leans on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms to discover and remediate security bugs across its software ecosystem. The monthly release addresses 70 “Critical” vulnerabilities, consisting of 57 Remote Code Execution flaws, 11 Elevation of Privilege issues and 2 spoofing bugs.The tally counts only updates released directly on Patch this week itself, excluding 348 separate flaws resolved earlier this month across Azure API Center, Azure App Service, Azure Event Grid, Azure SRE Agent, Mariner, Microsoft Bookings, Microsoft Dataverse, Microsoft Exchange Server and Microsoft Partner Center.Across the release, elevation of privilege and remote execution bugs made up the vast majority of the patched flaws:Microsoft defines a zero-day vulnerability as a flaw that has been publicly disclosed or actively exploited before an official patch exists. The October update resolves three such weaknesses. In one case, attackers actively exploited this flaw to evade Windows' “Mark of the Web” security mechanism.Microsoft warned that “improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Windows Shell allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network. ”The second local security bypass flaw was discovered by James Forshaw of Google Project Zero, and allows authenticated attackers to subvert Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) and launch unauthorized applications.Thirdly, the flaw is caused by improperly controlled sequential memory allocation within .NET, and enables unauthorised attackers to trigger a denial-of-service condition over a network. Microsoft did not disclose who reported the vulnerability.Alongside the security updates, Microsoft formally marked end-of-support milestones for multiple operating system editions:“Today, October 13, 2026, Windows 11, version 24H2 Home and Pro, and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016 have reached end of updates. The October 2026 monthly security update is the last update available for these editions,” Microsoft stated.
Article Summary: Microsoft has released its October 2026 Patch Tuesday security rollout, delivering fixes for a record-breaking 1,411 vulnerabilities. The huge volume of fixes comes as Microsoft increasingly leans on artificial intelligence (AI) platforms to discover and remediate security bugs. The monthly release addresses 70 “Critical” vulnerabilities, consisting of 57 Remote Code Execution flaws, 11 Elevation of Privilege issues and 2 spoofing bugs.

Article Title: Former Yahoo CEO and Google executive urges industry to acknowledge that things may not go well with AI: ‘What that really means is…’
Article Text:
Tech industry's ‘Cavalier’ rollout fueled public backlash

Marissa Mayer has said that the truth about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) is simple: nobody actually knows where it is heading. Speaking on stage of Fortune’s annual Most Powerful Women Summit in California, the former Yahoo CEO and longtime tech leader addressed the debates surrounding frontier AI labs, calling on the sector to embrace humility. Mayer emphasised that the uncertainty surrounding rapid AI development cuts in both directions, urging developers and policymakers to be candid about the potential risks.“We have a new form of intelligence, and anyone who says they know how this is going to play out is either lying or arrogant or both,” Mayer said, adding, “We have to acknowledge that there is a possibility that things won’t go well,” she noted. However, Mayer put the probability of a genuinely negative outcome at “well less than 50%,” observing that even several prominent AI doomers would likely agree with that calculation.“What that really means is the odds are in our favor,” Mayer explained, pointing to transformative upsides such as major medical breakthroughs, scientific discoveries, and “freeing people up to spend their time and live their lives the way they want to.”While describing herself as an optimist, Mayer welcomed ongoing discussions regarding official regulation as well as technical collaboration among competing frontier labs as their models advance.Mayer also addressed the shifting cultural tide, conceding that public sentiment across the United States has increasingly soured on AI and that the tech sector itself deserves much of the blame. The initial corporate positioning of the technology was “perhaps too cavalier,” Mayer observed, leaving working people uneasy about what enterprise-wide AI adoption will mean for their jobs, their households, and their children's economic futures.Despite those widespread anxieties, Mayer expressed confidence in the technology's ultimate potential, telling Brady: “I personally think it can make all three of those things better.”Mayer's perspective comes from decades at the center of consumer technology. After joining Google as an early software engineer and rising to become one of its most visible top executives, she was appointed CEO of Yahoo in 2012, making her the youngest female chief executive of a Fortune 500 company at the time.Her tenure drew public scrutiny, including criticism over her decision to take a brief maternity leave.
Article Summary: Former Yahoo CEO Marissa Mayer spoke at Fortune's Most Powerful Women Summit. She said that nobody knows where artificial intelligence (AI) is heading. Mayer said that the probability of a genuinely negative outcome is “well less than 50%.” She welcomed ongoing discussions regarding official regulation.

Article Title: How Canon EOS R6 V camera and Pixma G3770 printer can help you preserve Durga Puja and Dussehra memories
Article Text:
Canon camera and printer for Durga Puja and Dussehra memories: Price in India

Product Price Canon EOS R6 V Rs 2,35,995 Canon Pixma G3770 Rs 20,270

Canon EOS R6 V: Key highlights

Canon Pixma G3770: Key highlights

Article Summary: The Canon EOS R6 V and Canon Pixma G3770 serve different needs, from capturing photos and videos to printing memories at home. Article Title: Apple iPhone Duo goes on pre-order in India: Price, offers, where to buy and more
Article Text:
Apple iPhone Duo : Price in India

Where to buy Apple iPhone Duo

Launch offers and discounts

What the phone offers

Apple has opened pre-orders for the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone, in India, marking the company's entry into the rapidly growing foldable device segment. The smartphone is available for pre-order starting today (October 16) and the sale will begin starting October 23. The iPhone Duo was unveiled at Apple's "Surprise and Shine" event in September and features a foldable design with a 5.4-inch outer display that unfolds into a 7.6-inch inner screen. The device is powered by the A20 Pro chip and comes with a dual rear camera system.Apple has launched the foldable smartphone in four storage variants:* 256GB: Rs 2,99,900* 512GB: Rs 3,24,900* 1TB: Rs 3,74,900* 2TB: Rs 4,49,900The smartphone will be available in Star White and Night Sky colour options.Customers can pre-order the iPhone Duo through the Apple Online Store, the Apple Store app, Apple retail stores and select authorised retail partners across India. The device is also expected to be available through partner retailers, although availability may vary by channel.Apple is offering several launch benefits for buyers of the iPhone Duo in India:* Instant cashback of up to Rs 7,000 on eligible American Express, Axis Bank and ICICI Bank cards.* No-cost EMI options for up to 12 months on eligible purchases.* Apple Trade In benefits of up to Rs 81,500 on eligible devices, depending on their model and condition.* Three months of Apple Music, Apple TV+ and Apple Arcade subscriptions for eligible customers.The Duo has a 7.6-inch inner display with a nano-texture finish to reduce glare. Its 5.4-inch outer display delivers 90 percent of the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro. Both screens share the same aspect ratio. Apple calls it the thinnest iPhone ever when open. It is powered by the new A20 Pro chip, with a vapour chamber for cooling and a dual-battery design.The frame is titanium, the device has an IP68 rating, and Touch ID is built into the side button. A custom hinge made of more than 100 components holds the display flat when open.
Article Summary: Apple has opened pre-orders for the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone, in India. The smartphone is available for pre-order starting today (October 16) and the sale will begin starting October 23. Article Title: LinkedIn is testing a feed without strangers, and India is among the first to get it
Article Text:
LinkedIn tests new Network feed in India, US, UK and Australia

LinkedIn wants your connections to matter after you hit Connect

LinkedIn is testing a new feed that keeps strangers out. Called the Network feed, it pulls together posts only from your connections and the people you follow, and India is among the first countries to get it.The idea is to separate updates from people you know from the rest of the main feed, which is often crowded with viral career advice and posts from accounts you never chose to see. The test begins in the US, India, the UK and Australia, and LinkedIn has not shared a timeline for a wider rollout.There is a small catch. Since followed accounts are included, the feed is not strictly limited to people you have met. Follow a handful of creators and they will still sit alongside your former colleagues.The Network feed is part of a wider push around professional relationships. LinkedIn says its research shows more than half of Gen Z are unsure what to do after connecting with someone.Its answer includes digital business cards you can customise and add to your phone's wallet, rolling out globally over the coming months. Premium subscribers can now add private notes to profiles, recording where they met someone and when to reconnect.Authors can also pin useful comments under their posts.The rest of the update is about side hustles. LinkedIn says founders on the platform are up 70%, and over 80% of its creators post alongside another role. A new creator dashboard, found by tapping your profile picture in the app, reaches all markets in the coming weeks.Two earning tools are US-only for now. In-Stream Ads, which pays eligible creators when pre-roll ads run on their videos, is a limited test. Advice Sessions lets Business Premium subscribers sell paid 1:1 consultations from their profiles, with more markets promised.
Article Summary: Network feed pulls together posts only from your connections and people you follow. Test begins in the US, India, the UK and Australia, and LinkedIn has not shared a timeline for a wider rollout. LinkedIn says its research shows more than half of Gen Z are unsure what to do after connecting with someone.

Article Title: UK may make viewers pay to watch Netflix, Amazon, Disney Plus, YouTube and other streaming platforms; here's what proposed 'YouTube tax' is
Article Text:
Representational image

Streaming has become the easiest way around the BBC licence fee

No final decision on the YouTube tax has been made yet

Watching YouTube in the UK could soon come with a bill. The British government is reportedly preparing to extend the BBC licence fee, the £180 yearly charge households pay to watch live TV, to cover streaming platforms such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney Plus and YouTube.The plan is expected to be part of a government white paper on renewing the BBC's royal charter, due before Christmas. It has already picked up an unofficial nickname, the "YouTube tax", since YouTube is Britain's biggest online video platform with around 55 million users and a 79% reach in the market.At present, the licence fee applies to anyone watching live TV on any device, or using BBC iPlayer. On-demand viewing on other services is exempt, so a household that only streams Netflix or YouTube pays nothing. A senior government source said people are using these platforms to dodge the fee, and called it unfair that viewers can watch TV content without paying for it.The numbers show why the government is moving now. Around 539,000 fewer TV licences were in force in the year to March 31, 2026, and the total has dropped by roughly two million over five years. The BBC collects about £3.8 billion to £3.9 billion from the fee, yet still posted an operating deficit of £121 million for 2025/26.Bringing streaming under the fee could add an estimated 3 to 4 million paying households. That money, however, is not meant to fill the BBC's budget gaps. It is expected to fund local journalism and efforts against misinformation, which the source linked to the rise of parties such as Reform UK.The BBC has been asking for reform too. Director-general Matt Brittin has called the current model outdated and said BBC content should be on Netflix, YouTube, TikTok and Spotify. The broadcaster also plans to bring its news channel to YouTube.The Department for Culture, Media and Sport, led by Lisa Nandy, said it is weighing a range of options for the licence fee and that nothing has been decided.Earlier this month, a cross-party committee of MPs recommended that the fee should no longer be tied to live TV or a television set. It also suggested the cost could come down if more people pay. About 94% of people use the BBC every month, but only 80% of households hold a licence.Existing concessions, including free licences for over-75s on pension credit and a 50% discount for visually impaired viewers, are part of the current system. How a streaming-era fee would be collected, and whether platforms or households would foot the bill, is still unclear.The current charter expires in December 2027, so British viewers should know well before then whether their YouTube habit comes with a price.
Article Summary: Streaming has become the easiest way around the BBC licence fee. A senior government source said people are using these platforms to dodge the fee, and called it unfair that viewers can watch TV content without paying for it. The Department for Culture, Media and Sport said it is weighing a range of options and nothing has been decided.

Article Title: NetApp launches 15th Excellerator cohort focused on AI, deep-tech startups
Article Text: Data infrastructure company Vasanthi Ramesh-led NetApp India has launched the 15th cohort of its startup accelerator programme, NetApp Excellerator, selecting five deep-tech startups working in areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, workflow automation and enterprise data intelligence. The latest cohort brings together startups from India, the United States and Israel that are building technologies aimed at helping enterprises deploy AI at scale. The programme is designed to provide founders with access to NetApp's technology leaders, mentorship, data infrastructure expertise and opportunities to explore proof-of-concept (PoC) engagements.The five startups selected for Cohort 15 are LightSprint AI, an AI-native software engineering platform; Wald.ai, which offers semantic data loss prevention for AI communications; Lasso Security, a cybersecurity platform focused on securing generative AI applications and large language models; Cogover, a no-code and low-code workflow automation platform; and QUIPU AI, a knowledge intelligence platform that helps enterprises convert data into AI-ready contextual intelligence.The company said the new cohort reflects growing enterprise demand for technologies that support AI deployment, security, automation and intelligent data infrastructure."AI is still altering industries and opening up new opportunities for businesses all over the world," said Vasanthi Ramesh, Vice President of Engineering and Site Leader at NetApp India. She added that the selected startups are addressing key challenges enterprises face while deploying AI at scale and that the accelerator programme aims to help founders transform innovative ideas into scalable products through technical guidance, mentorship and enterprise opportunities.Two startups in the cohort, Cogover and QUIPU AI, are part of ExcellerateHER, NetApp's initiative to support women-founded and women-led startups. The company said the programme has supported 23 women-led startups since its launch. Naren Meadem, founder and CEO of QUIPU AI, said participation in the accelerator would help the company validate its technology in enterprise environments and explore how its long-term memory capabilities can support AI initiatives at scale.Meanwhile, Mina Nguyen, co-founder and chief growth officer of Cogover, said the company aims to simplify business workflows by connecting data, applications and processes on a single platform, enabling people and AI systems to work from the same information.NetApp said its accelerator programme has supported 90 startups across 14 previous cohorts since its launch in 2017. Participating companies have collectively raised more than $600 million in funding, while the programme has facilitated 30 proof-of-concept engagements and resulted in six commercial contracts with NetApp.Each cohort runs for six months, during which startups collaborate with NetApp teams on potential use cases and PoCs. Selected startups also receive a $15,000 grant to support potential proof-of-concept projects. The latest cohort underscores the growing focus among enterprise technology companies on fostering AI-driven innovation as organisations increasingly invest in intelligent data infrastructure and next-generation software platforms.
Article Summary: NetApp India has launched the 15th cohort of its startup accelerator programme, NetApp Excellerator. Five deep-tech startups working in areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, workflow automation and enterprise data intelligence. The latest cohort brings together startups from India, the United States and Israel.
